validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed independently and repeatedly -- FERC Docket CP21-465 (Federal Register notice of application, 2021-07-07: Driftwood Pipeline LLC filed 2021-06-17 for dual 42-in pipelines, Beauregard/Calcasieu Parishes LA; FERC issued the certificate 2023-04-21), EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (row for 'Driftwood Line 200 and 300 Project Phase 1'), and Williams' own project fact sheet (Line 200, $1.9B, ~37 mi, 3.1 Bcf/d, joint venture with Woodside). Not a GEM-only entity. CLASSIFICATION: correct -- an interstate NGA section 7(c)-certificated transmission pipeline (FERC-jurisdictional, not gathering), Fuel=Gas is correct. DUPLICATE/FAMILY: the batch prompt flags 4 Driftwood-family rows (P0177 mainline 99.3mi/CP17-117+118; P3282/P7770/P7769 = Line 200+300 Phases 1/2/3/CP21-465) as needing a duplicate check. Confirmed NOT duplicates: P0177 is the ~96-99 mi FEED-GAS pipeline from a Columbia Gulf interconnect near Ville Platte LA to the LNG terminal (separate docket, separate certificate issued 2019, EIA rows for it list CP17-117/CP17-118), while P3282/P7770/P7769 are three sequential build-out phases of a SEPARATE, later-certificated (CP21-465, 2023) pair of pipelines (Line 200 + Line 300) that add takeaway capacity FROM Haynesville-area supply points TO the terminal/interconnects near Carlyss LA, per EIA: Phase 1 (P3282) = ~36.9 mi of Line 200 (Ragley, Beauregard Parish -> receiver facility near Carlyss, Calcasieu Parish) + the Indian Bayou Compressor Station's initial units; Phase 2 (P7770, EIA) = remainder of Line 300 (~31-32 mi) + additional compressor units; Phase 3 (P7769, EIA) = remaining compressor units only (no new pipe). A mainline (P0177) figure is never a ref for a phase row and vice versa -- respected throughout this shard. CORPORATE HISTORY (verify lead confirmed): the terminal and its pipeline family changed hands -- Tellurian Inc. was 100% owner as of the 2023-04-21 FERC order (see Tellurian's own 2023-04-24 press release, Wayback-captured); Woodside Energy acquired Tellurian in 2024 and renamed the LNG terminal 'Louisiana LNG' (Woodside's own project page, Wayback-captured 2026, lists 'Woodside completes acquisition of Tellurian' and 'Woodside to acquire Tellurian and Driftwood LNG' among its news items); most recently Williams (The Williams Companies) and Woodside formed a joint venture (effective 2025-01-01 per Williams' own fact sheet, which is dated with a 2025/2026 print code) under which Williams holds 80% ownership and is the operator of the Line 200 project specifically, Woodside retaining 20% -- see the attribution concern below and cross_row_leads for the mainline (P0177).
